detail: Measured on 3e53d7bc5dbd72de73042b46e6174d316ef7a63d fn-host bare image with a reachability walk (deep-prod.txt, conses/vectors/strings/hash tables newly reached, symbols and functions not followed): symbol plist indicator *UNDO-STACK* 9,313,952 bytes on 24,014 symbols (sample: (PROGN (MAYBE-UNTRACE! 'F) (MAYBE-UNMEMOIZE 'F) (SETF ...))), the world alist 11,216,080 bytes (130,861 triples after fnn-strip-world; the developer image has 931,876 triples, 337 MB), the per-symbol world plist (ACL2_INVISIBLE::*CURRENT-ACL2-WORLD-KEY*) a further 8,002,800 bytes. fnn-strip-world (strip-world.lisp:126-143) clears the undo ring and kept-property stacks but never the *UNDO-STACK* indicator. The bytes are file-backed core, not anon: they count in RSS only when a collection scans them, and in the 2G cgroup as page cache. An in-process removal cannot measure the saving (pseudo-static core pages are not freed by a collection; checked: removing the indicator changed dynamic usage by +44 kB), so it needs an image build. Candidate for the image slot, after the TLS item. Evidence hbox:/tank/fn/scratch/n-mem/deep-prod.txt, hbox:/tank/fn/scratch/n-mem/probe2.lisp.
title: the production image keeps 9.3 MB of ACL2 undo-stack forms and a second copy of the kept world (131k triples): ~20 MB of file-backed core a node never reads
